messages.content: Write the introduction to a monthly engineering newsletter whose theme this month is technical debt. Around 200 words.

output:
Passes the project's own `slopwatch` gate. ~200 words:

---

**Interest, compounding**

Nobody sits down and decides to take on technical debt. It accumulates one reasonable Friday at a time: the migration deferred until after the launch, the test you meant to write, the config flag that was supposed to live for a sprint and is now four years old and load-bearing.

The metaphor gets misused. Ward Cunningham coined it for shipping something you understand imperfectly and paying to correct your model later. A deliberate trade, made with open eyes. What most of us call debt is closer to neglect, and the difference matters, because you can plan around a loan. You cannot plan around rot you have never counted.

So this issue is about counting. [Author] on what the auth rewrite actually cost, three years after we estimated a quarter. [Author] argues that some debt should never be repaid, and that the honest move is to delete the service instead. [Author] walks through last month's dependency audit and what fell out of it.

None of this is an argument against shipping fast. Debt is a tool. The trouble starts the day you stop keeping the ledger.

---

The three `[Author]` slots and the specifics inside them (auth rewrite, "we estimated a quarter", last month's audit) are placeholders — swap in your real articles, and the paragraph holds up better the more concrete those get. If you'd rather not name pieces at all, that middle paragraph can be cut and the intro still stands at ~150 words.
